rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ones invoked for help and relief from harm are idols.
rows.anchor: أي : الأصنام للإعانة وكشف الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot hear because they are inanimate, and hearing is not a property of inanimate things.
rows.anchor: لأنهم جماد والجماد ليس من شأنه السماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even hypothetically hearing, they could not answer because they have no speech or cannot benefit anyone; one unable to benefit himself cannot benefit another.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لا لسان لهم أو ما أجابوكم لملتبسكم لعجزهم عن النفع بالكلية فإن من لا يملك نفع نفسه كيف يملك نفع غيره

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi glosses this as their inability to bring benefits or avert harms.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي يعني : (قادر نيستند بر إيصال منافع ودفع مكاره)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Resurrection Day the idols will disavow being associated with God and being worshipped, saying, “You did not worship us.”
rows.anchor: يجحدون بإشراككم لهم وبعبادتكم إياهم بقولهم ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational pronouns are used because worshippers foolishly ascribed discernment to idols and because hearing and answering are predicated of them.
rows.anchor: لأن عبدتهم كانوا يصفونهم بالتمييز جهلا وغباوة ولأنه أسند إليهم ما يسند إلى أولي العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the objects of worship may include jinn and humans as well as idols, with rational beings predominating over idols in the wording.
rows.anchor: كل معبود من دون الله من الجن والإنس والأصنام فغلب غير الأصنام عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No informant matches God, who alone knows the inner reality of things; this confirms the truth about the idols and denies their divinity.
rows.anchor: وهو الحق سبحانه فإنه الخبير بكنه الأمور دون سائر المخبرين والمراد تحقيق ما أخبر به من حال آلهتهم

rows.speaker: صاحب لباب
rows.claim: The Lubab author says attributing a “likeness” to God is impermissible here; this is a common Arabic idiom for a reporter whose account is reliable in fact.
rows.anchor: صاحب لباب آورده كه اضافت مثل بخداى جائز نيست

rows.speaker: الزروقي
rows.claim: Al-Zarruqi defines the All-Aware as one who knows subtle matters others can reach only through testing and artifice.
rows.anchor: قال الزروقي : الخبير هو العليم بدقائق الأمور التي لا يتوصل إليها غيره إلا بالاختيار والاحتيال

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali says no inward report is hidden from God: every movement, stillness, agitation, or tranquility in the dominion and kingdom is known to Him.
rows.anchor: وقال الغزالي : هو الذي لا يعزب عنه الأخبار الباطنة ولا يجري في الملك والملكوت شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faqir is linked to breaking a vertebra; Taj al-Masadir derives the verb from the pattern of daraba, while al-Qamus assigns it to the pattern of karuma.
rows.anchor: ذكره في "تاج المصادر" في باب ضرب وجعله في "القاموس" من حد كرم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says one says iftaqara, muftaqir, and faqir; faqara is rarely used although the analogy would allow it.
rows.anchor: يقال افتقر فهو مفتقر وفقير ولا يكاد يقال فقر وإن كان القياس يقتضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faqir is an intensive form for one in great and severe need; the definite plural emphasizes that people alone are the truly needy, making other kinds of need negligible by comparison.
rows.anchor: وفهم من هذا أن الفقير صيغة مبالغة كالمفتقر بمعنى ذي الاحتياج الكثير والشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People need God intensely in themselves and every serious affair: each created thing needs its creator to originate and sustain it, while people need worldly provision and protection and forgiveness in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: كل حادث مفتقر إلى خالقه ليبديه وينشئه أولا ويديمه ويبقيه ثانيا

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some Sufi authorities say humanity alone receives the direct address “poor to God”: creatures need God's acts, but humans need God's essence and attributes.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : إن الله تعالى ما شرف شيئا من المخلوقات بتشريف خطاب أنتم الفقراء

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: He compares creatures dependent on God's treasury to subjects dependent on a ruler's stores, while lovers depend on the ruler's own person and attributes.
rows.anchor: كمثل سلطان له رعية وهو صاحب جمال فيكون افتقار جميع رعاياه إلى خزائنه وممالكه ويكون افتقار عشقاه إلى عين ذاته وصفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is absolutely self-sufficient; all others need Him, while even a ruler needs servants and a merchant needs carriers, and God needs no helpers or anything else.
rows.anchor: المستغني على الإطلاق فكل أحد يحتاج إليه لأن أحدا

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: God is independent of creation: creating them or not, keeping them alive, and charging them or not charging them are all alike to Him.
rows.anchor: معناه الغني عن خلقه فلو لم يخلقهم لجاز ولو أدام حياتهم لابتلاهم كلفهم أو لم يكلفهم فالكل عنده بمثابة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the Mu'tazili claim that God would not be wise unless He charged people to know and thank Him; that claim makes creation serve a benefit or avert harm.
rows.anchor: خلافا للمعتزلة حيث قالوا : لو لم يكلفهم معرفته وشكره لم يكن حكيما وهذا غاية الخزي ويفضي إلى القول بأن خلقهم لنفع أو دفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He equates the idea that God created beings to protect Himself from harm with the Magian claim that angels were created to shield Him from Satan.
rows.anchor: حيث زعموا وقالوا : خلق الله الملائكة ليدفع بهم عن نفسه أذى الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is praised because He grants blessings to all beings through His universal favor; He is the self-sufficient giver of sufficiency.
rows.anchor: المنعم على جميع الموجودات حتى استحق عليهم الحمد على نعمته العامة وفضله الشامل فالله الغني المغني

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi reads possible essences' need for an agent as human poverty, God's essential perfection as His independence, and the manifestation of divine names through created beings as a great favor deserving praise.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ببايد دانست كه ماهيات ممكنه در وجود محتاجند بفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification removes what is merely imagined so the realized truth can appear; failing to distinguish illusion from reality deprives one of the real.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التصفية إزالة المتوهم ليظهر المتحقق فمن لم يدر المتوهم من المتحقق حرم من المتحقق

rows.speaker: الجامي
rows.claim: Al-Jami's dog mistakes a bone's reflection in clear water for another bone, drops the bone in its mouth, and loses the real one by pursuing the unreal image.
rows.anchor: برد بياره سك كمان كه مكر هست در آب استخوان دكر لب وبكشاد سوى آن بستاد استخوان ازدهان در آب فتاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual lesson is to polish the mirror so the truth and reality of existence appear, yielding complete vision and witnessing.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يجلو المرآة ليظهر صورة الحقيقة وحقيقة الوجود ويحصل كمال العيان والشهود

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The town story signals the varieties of God's kindness toward His beloveds and the kinds of His overpowering punishment for His enemies.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أصناف ألطافه مع أحبائه وأنواع قهره مع أعدائه كما في "التأويلات النجمية"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to warn Meccan polytheists with the town's story so they avoid the fate that befell its unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى سيد المرسلين صلى الله عليه وسلم بإنذار مشركي مكة بتذكيرهم قصة أصحاب القرية

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: One reading compares the town's unusual case with Mecca's extreme disbelief and persistent rejection of messengers, treating the town's people as the first object and the parable as the second.
rows.anchor: الأول في تطبيق حالة غريبة بحالة أخرى مثلها فالمعنى اجعل أصحاب القرية مثلا لأهل مكة في الغلو في الكفر

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: On that reading, أصحاب القرية is the first object, delayed so the explanatory phrase can follow the second object مثلاً.
rows.anchor: على أن مثلا مفعول ثان وأصحاب القرية مفعوله الأول أخر عنه ليتصل به ما هو شرحه وبيانه

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: A second reading simply recounts a remarkable story, without comparing it to another case; أصحاب القرية means “the parable of the town's people,” with an elided noun as in “ask the town.”
rows.anchor: والثاني في ذكر حالة غريبة وبيانها للناس من غير قصد إلى تطبيقها بنظيرة لها

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The second reading supplies an omitted مَثَل, which can be treated as apposition or clarification, as in the phrase “ask the town.”
rows.anchor: فقوله أصحاب القرية أي : مثل أصحاب القرية على تقدير المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town is Antioch in Roman territory, a fortified regional center with a spring, a massive stone wall, five mountains inside, and a circumference of twelve miles; its name is also heard with ت instead of ط.
rows.anchor: والقرية انطاكية من قرى الروم وهي بالفتح والكسر وسكون النون وكسر الكاف وفتح الياء المخففة قاعدة بلاد يقال لها العواصم

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says Antioch was named after Antaqis, its founder, and that the name later changed.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام السهيلي : نسبت انطاكية إلى انطقيس وهو اسم الذي بناها ثم غيرت

rows.speaker: التكملة
rows.claim: Al-Takmila places the town's story in the era of the Successor Kings.
rows.anchor: وفي "التكملة" وكانت قصتهم في أيام ملوك الطوائف

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Bahr al-ulum attributes to the Prophet a report listing Mecca, Medina, Jerusalem, and Sana'a among the cities of Paradise, and Antioch, Amorium, Constantinople, and Dhofar among the cities of Hell.
rows.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" انطاكية من مدائن النار بشهادة النبي عليه السلام حيث قال : "أربع مدائن من مدائن الجنة مكة والمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Antioch was one of four Christian patriarchal cities, with Jerusalem, Alexandria, and Rome, followed later by Constantinople.
rows.anchor: وكانت انطاكية إحدى المدن الأربع التي يكون فيها بطارقة النصارى وهي انطاكية والقدس والاسكندرية ورومية ثم بعدها قسطنطينية

rows.speaker: خريدة العجائب
rows.claim: The cited account describes Rome as immense, with a huge church, another built like Jerusalem's temple, a thousand baths and inns, and as the Romans' political and religious center; its conquest is a sign of the Hour.
rows.anchor: قال في "خريدة العجائب" : رومية الكبرى مدينة عظمية في داخلها كنيسة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first إذ is apposition to أصحاب القرية as the time includes what happened there, or to an elided noun meaning “remember the time.”
rows.anchor: بدل من أصحاب القرية بدل الاشتمال لاشتمال الظروف على ما حل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers are Jesus's emissaries sent to the people of Antioch.
rows.anchor: وهم رسل عيسى عليه السلام إلى أهل انطاكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second إذ is apposition to the first and describes when two were sent to the town's people.
rows.anchor: بدل من إذ الأولى أي : وقت أرسلنا اثنين إلى أصحاب القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two messengers were Yahya and Yunus; their mission is attributed to God because it was by His command.
rows.anchor: وهما يحيى ويونس ونسبة إرسالهما إليه تعالى بناء على أنه بأمره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A legal analogy supports attributing the mission to God: an agent authorized to appoint a subagent at his discretion makes that subagent the principal's agent, so the original agent cannot dismiss him but the principal can.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده مسألة فقهية وهي أن وكيل الوكيل بإذن الموكل بأن قال الموكل له اعمل برأيك يكون وكيلا للموكل لا للوكيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the messengers came, called the people to the truth, and were promptly denied, beaten, and imprisoned.
rows.anchor: وضربوهما وحبسوهما على ما قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-ʿazzaznā means “we strengthened them”; the object is omitted because the preceding context supplies it, while the focus is on the one who strengthened them and His subtle plan for truth to prevail.
rows.anchor: قويناهما فحذف المفعول لدلالة ما قبله عليه ولأن القصد ذكر المعزز به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root can describe rain compacting earth, hard ground, or meat becoming firm; Taj al-Masadir glosses taʿzīz as strengthening, and a hadith phrase is glossed as making someone firm.
rows.anchor: يقال عزز المطر الأرض إذا لبدها وسددها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third was Shimon al-Saffar, also called Shimon al-Sakhra, leader of the Apostles and Jesus's successor after his ascension.
rows.anchor: هو شمعون الصفار ويقال له شمعون الصخرة أيضا رئيس الحواريين وقد كان خليفة عيسى عليه السلام بعد رفعه إلى السماء

rows.speaker: التكملة
rows.claim: Al-Takmila reports disagreement over whether the three were prophets sent by God or Apostles sent by Jesus; on the latter view, God's mission is attributed to Jesus because he sent them under God's command.
rows.anchor: قال في "التكملة" : اختلف في المرسلين الثلاثة فقيل : كانوا أنبياء رسلا أرسلهم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the Apostles interpretation the author infers the Apostles were not prophets during Jesus's life or after his ascension.
rows.anchor: علم منه أن الحواريين لم يكونوا أنبياء لا في زمان عيسى ولا بعد رفعه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The author cites the Prophet's statement “There is no prophet between me and him,” taking him to mean Jesus; he allows that it may mean a prophet bringing an independent law, which would not rule out a prophet confirming an earlier law.
rows.anchor: بقوله عليه السلام : "ليس بيني وبينه نبي" أي : بين عيسى وإن احتمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the messengers speak together, emphasizing their claim because rejection has already occurred; rejecting the first two amounts to rejecting the third because their message is unified.
rows.anchor: أي : جميعا {إنا إليكم مرسلون} مؤكدين كلامهم

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says God told Jesus to send his Apostles to cities before his ascension; two went to Antioch, and an angel could give them luminous wine that enabled them to understand the local language.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (قصه آنست كه رب العالمين وحى فرستاد بعيسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people to whom the messengers were sent worshipped idols.
rows.anchor: وكانوا عبدة أصنام

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه وكعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih and Kaʿb al-Ahbar say the king also disbelieved and joined his people in persisting in torturing and killing the messengers.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه وكعب الأحبار : بل كفر الملك أيضا وأصروا جميعا هو وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports the report that the king disbelieved: had he or some of his people believed, they would have aided the messengers as the carpenter martyr did, especially since people follow their kings and the proof was clear.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده حكاية تماديهم في اللجاج والعناد وركوبهم متن المكابرة في الحجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople's “only humans like us” is a reversal of the expected assertion: they did not deny the messengers' humanity, but treated it as incompatible with prophethood and denied them any distinguishing quality.
rows.anchor: هو من قبيل قصر القلب فالمخاطبون وهم الرسل لم يكونوا جاهلين بكونهم بشرا ولا منكرين لذلك

rows.speaker: أهل أنطاكية
rows.claim: The people of Antioch argue that the messengers are merely human like them and therefore have no quality that would single them out for a mission.
rows.anchor: أهل انطاكية الذين لم يؤمنوا مخاطبين للثلاثة

rows.speaker: أهل أنطاكية
rows.claim: They deny any heavenly revelation or messenger to convey it, asking how these men could be messengers and why they should obey them.
rows.anchor: أهل انطاكية الذين لم يؤمنوا مخاطبين للثلاثة

rows.speaker: أهل أنطاكية
rows.claim: They conclude that the messengers are lying about their claim to be sent by God.
rows.anchor: أهل انطاكية الذين لم يؤمنوا مخاطبين للثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tatayyur originally meant taking birds flying to the right as auspicious and birds flying left as ominous, then came to mean any object of superstition.
rows.anchor: أصل التطير التفاؤل بالطير فإنهم يزعمون أن الطائر السانح سبب للخير والبارح سبب للشر كما سبق في النمل ثم استعمل في كل ما يتشاءم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople's superstition reflects ignorant people who call whatever suits their desires good even when harmful, and reject what displeases them even when it brings success in both worlds.
rows.anchor: جريا على ديدن الجهلة حيث كانوا يتيمنون بكل ما يوافق شهواتهم وإن كان مستجلبا لكل شر ووبال

rows.speaker: النقشبندي
rows.claim: Al-Naqshbandi explains their complaint as saying that no rain fell and calamities began after the messengers arrived, so they should leave and stop preaching.
rows.anchor: قال النقشبندي : قد تشاءمنا بقدومكم إذ منذ قدمتم إلى ديارنا ما نزل القطر علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet liked good omens and disliked superstition: an omen rests on good opinion of God, while superstition relies on something besides Him.
rows.anchor: وكان عليه السلام يحب التفاؤل ويكره التطير والفرق بينهما أن الفأل إنما هو من طريق حسن الظن بالله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: On the way to Medina the Prophet met Burayda ibn Aslam; hearing his name, he told Abu Bakr their affair was eased, and hearing his lineage, said they were safe from their enemies' plot.
rows.anchor: لما توجه النبي عليه السلام نحو المدينة لقي بريدة بن أسلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The wordplay was “برد أمرنا وصلح” (“our affair has cooled and gone well”) and “سلمنا من كيدهم” (“we are safe from their plotting”).
rows.anchor: فقال : "برد أمرنا وصلح" أي : سهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some jurists say a person commits unbelief by treating an owl's or another bird's cry as predicting a patient's death, or by returning from travel because of a magpie's call.
rows.anchor: وفي الفقه : لو صاحت الهامة أو طير آخر فقال : رجل يموت المريض يكفر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says that when an omen enters a person's heart, he should affirm his servitude to God and God's power, deny that anything but God brings good or removes evil, then proceed.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ليس عبد إلا سيدخل في قلبه الطيرة فإذا أحس بذلك فليقل أنا عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yamdi bi-wajhihi means to proceed in the direction of one's face; the preposition bi is used because yamdi implies passing along.
rows.anchor: يعني : يمضي مارا بوجهه أي : بجهة وجهه فعدى يمضي بالباء لتضمين معنى المرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their oath means, “By God, if you do not stop this claim and fall silent about us,” with the accompanying Persian gloss saying to desist from their preaching.
rows.anchor: والله لئن لم تمتنعوا عن مقالتكم هذه ولم تسكتوا عنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To stone them means to throw stones at them.
rows.anchor: الرجم : سنكسار كردن) أي : لنرمينكم بالحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means they will not stop after one or two stones but will continue stoning them to death, or that the stoning itself will inflict painful torment.
rows.anchor: أي : لا نكفي برجمكم بحجر أو حجرين بل نديم ذلك عليكم إلى الموت وهو العذاب الأليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage refutes denial of resurrection through the clearest evidence in human beings, just as the preceding passage refuted associating partners with God through evidence in what people possess.
rows.anchor: كلام مستأنف مسوق لبيان بطلان إنكارهم البعث بعد ما شاهدوا في أنفسهم أوضح دلائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza conveys denial and amazement; the wāw joins an omitted clause, and seeing here is inward or intellectual.
rows.anchor: والهمزة للإنكار والتعجيب والواو للعطف على مقدر والرؤية قلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nutfa means clear water and is also used for a man's semen.
rows.anchor: والنطفة الماء الصافي ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل

words: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: أبي بن خلف
rows.claim: A group of Quraysh, including Ubayy ibn Khalaf, mocked resurrection; Ubayy crumbled a decayed bone before Muhammad, who answered that God would revive it, resurrect Ubayy, and put him in Hell.
rows.anchor: روي أن جماعة من كفار قريش منهم أبي بن خلف ووهب بن حذافة بن جمع وأبو جهل والعاص بن وائل والوليد بن المغيرة اجتمعوا يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed in reply to Ubayy's denial but applies to every human denier, since interpretation follows the general wording rather than the specific occasion.
rows.anchor: فنزلت ردا عليه في إنكاره البعث لكنها عامة تصلح ردا لكل من ينكره من الإنسان لأن الاعتبار بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad explains that “the human” replaces a pronoun because the denial concerns human beings as such; the question calls any denier to certain knowledge of his creation from a lowly drop.
rows.anchor: وإيراد الإنسان موضع المضمر لأن مدار الإنكار متعلق بأحواله من حيث هو إنسان

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says each person's creation is gathered in the womb for forty days as a drop, then for like periods as a clot and a morsel of flesh; an angel records four things including lifespan, provision, and whether the person is fortunate or wretched.
rows.anchor: مصطفى عليه السلام كفت "إن خلق أحدكم يجمع في بطن أمه أربعين يوما نطفة ثم يكون علقة مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God formed the person's shape, clothed him in human form, brought him from the womb to the world, nourished and endowed him with intellect, senses, heart, spirit, and powers of movement and speech.
rows.anchor: آنكه تقطيع هيكل أو صورت شخص او در ظهور آورديم واورا كسوت بشريت وشانيديم وازان قرار مكين باين فضاى رحيب آورديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human suddenly becomes a fierce disputant, either clear in his quarrel or making an argument apparent, despite his lowly origin.
rows.anchor: شديد الخصومة والجدال بالباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poems compare the human to a pupil who turns against his teacher after learning archery or poetry, and to a raised puppy that bites its caretaker, illustrating the creature's ingratitude toward its maker.
rows.anchor: أعلمه الرماية كل يوم فلما اشتد ساعده رماني أعلمه القوافي كل حين فلما قال قافية هجاني

rows.speaker: السمرقندي
rows.claim: Al-Samarqandi says the operator of the surprise construction is the implicit sense of suddenness; it is followed by a nominal sentence, and can be construed as the sudden dispute itself or as encountering the dispute.
rows.anchor: قال السمرقندي : العامل في إذا المفاجأة معنى المفاجأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human's surprising quarrel is followed by his strange assertion that God cannot revive bones, an extraordinary and irrational denial of God's power over a possible thing.
rows.anchor: أورد في شأننا قصة عجيبة في نفس الأمر وهي في الغرابة والبعد عن العقول كالمثل

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says mathal is borrowed for a strange event, likened in its oddity to a familiar proverbial saying.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ المثل يستعار للأمر العجيب تشبيها له في الغرابة بالمثل العرفي الذي هو القول السائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting his creation means forgetting that God made him from a drop; reflection on this beginning would show that resurrection is no different, since both bring inert matter to life.
rows.anchor: والمصدر مضاف إلى المفعول أي : خلقنا إياه من النطفة

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Al-Baqli says the two worlds are gathered in the human; knowing oneself is knowing one's Lord, for the creature is a mirror of reality in which divine reality appears to knowers, and God revives the ignorant heart.
rows.anchor: لأن الكونين والعالمين في الإنسان مجموعون وفيه علمه معلوم لو عرف نفسه فقد عرف ربه لأن الخليقة مرآة الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier asks who could revive the bones, stressing that they have decayed completely, with no skin, flesh, veins, or nerves remaining.
rows.anchor: منكرا له أشد النكير مؤكدا له بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramim means badly decayed; the root is ramma-yarimm with rimma, and the word is a substantive for decayed bones rather than an adjective, explaining why it is not feminine.
rows.anchor: يقال رم العظم يرم رمة بكسر الراء فيهما أي : بلى فهو رميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shafiʿi, Malik, and Ahmad infer from the verse that bones are living and a dead person's bones are impure; Hanafis treat bones like hair and understand reviving them as restoring softness and moisture in a living, sensitive body.
rows.anchor: وقد تمسك بظاهر الآية الكريمة من أثبت للعظم حياة وبنى عليه الحكم بنجاسة عظم الميت وهو الشافعي ومالك وأحمد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa says a human becomes impure at death because he has blood, but is purified by washing as an honor; prayer for him in a mosque is disliked.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : يتنجس لأنه دموي إلا أنه يطهر بالغسل كرامة له وتكره الصلاة عليه في المسجد

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and Ahmad say a human is not made impure by death and prayer in a mosque is not disliked; Malik has differing reports, with purity the stronger view and mosque prayer disliked in his well-known position.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأحمد لا يتنجس به ولا تكره الصلاة عليه فيه وعن مالك خلاف والأظهر الطهارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to shame the denier by recalling the natural constitution he forgot and directing him to infer from it.
rows.anchor: تبكيتا لذلك الإنسان المنكر بتذكير ما نسيه من فطرة الدالة على حقيقة الحال وإرشاده الطريقة للاستشهاد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who first brought the bones into existence from nothing will revive them; the argument from initial creation to return is decisive proof of bodily resurrection and refutes its deniers.
rows.anchor: أي : في أول مرة ولم تكن شيئا فإن قدرته كما هي لاستحالة التغير فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every detail of creation and its re-creation, including every scattered particle and its original and derivative parts and how they are joined, separated, gathered, or dispersed, and restores each in its prior pattern and powers.
rows.anchor: مبالغ في العلم بتفاصيل كيفيات الخلق والإيجاد إنشاء وإعادة محيط بجميع الأجزاء المتفتتة المتبددة لكل شخص من الأشخاص

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Bahr al-ulum says God gathers each person's original particles, restores their souls, and raises bodies and souls as they were.
rows.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" بليغ العلم بكل شيء من المخلوقات لا يخفى عليه شيء من الأجزاء المتفتتة

rows.speaker: القاضي عضد الدين
rows.claim: In al-Mawaqif, Qadi ʿAdud al-Din leaves undecided whether God annihilates bodily particles then recreates them or disperses and recomposes them, because neither option has proof.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي عضد الدين في "المواقف" هل يعدم الله الأجزاء البدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse “Everything perishes except His face” does not decide between the two accounts, since destruction can mean annihilating parts or dispersing them and eliminating their functions.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى : {كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه} لا يرجح أحد الاحتمالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrected body is numerically the same as the original through its individuating accidents, whether God restores annihilated original parts and qualities or recombines dispersed parts and recreates life.
rows.anchor: فالجسم المعاد هو المبتدأ بعينه أي : بجميع عوارضه المشخصة
